meta.title: Localization
meta.description: The seven built-in locale packs, how to override a message, and how to add a language of your own.

packs.intro: Every string the component shows, and every string it announces, comes from one object. Seven of them ship with the package; import the one you need from its own subpath so the others are not bundled:

messages.intro: A pack is a plain object, so replacing one message is a spread. Nothing is merged deeply for you: a nested group you touch has to be spread too, which is what keeps a typo from silently emptying a group.
points: Counts go through Intl.PluralRules, so a message with a count is an object of plural forms, not a string.
Placeholders are {{name}}, and the value is formatted in the pack’s own locale.
locale is what every date, time and number is formatted with — set it when you write a pack of your own.
dir: 'rtl' turns the whole layout around, without a second stylesheet.

adding.intro: A language of your own is one object that satisfies SchedulerLocalization. Start from the English pack so the type tells you what is still missing:
adding.formats: Dates, times and ranges are formatted by Intl from the pack’s locale, so a new language needs no format strings. formatters is there for the cases where a format has to differ from what Intl gives.
